ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-01.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-01.body:
The line $y=3$ is a horizontal axis of symmetry. The vertex $(3,3)$ lies on it, so it is the apex, and the other two vertices are mirror images in $y=3$. The reflection of $(5,2)$ is $(5,4)$.

**Answer: $(5,4)$**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-02.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-02.body:
The bat is awake $3$ of 24 hours: $\frac{3}{24}=\frac18=12.5\%$.

**Answer: 12.5%**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-03.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-03.body:
1. False: the single-digit primes are $2,3,5,7$ (four).
2. False: $9\text{ cm}^2=0.0009\text{ m}^2$.
3. True: H and I have rotational symmetry of order 2 (C, M and E have none).
4. True: $\frac78=0.875<0.889=\frac89$ (cross-multiply: $63<64$).

Two are true.

**Answer: 2**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-04.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-04.body:
The positive terms are $1,3,5,7$ and the negative terms are $-2,-4,-6,-8$. The largest is $7$ and the smallest is $-8$, so the range is $7-(-8)=15$.

**Answer: 15**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-05.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-05.body:
The calculator interprets the key presses as $2+4\div12\times6+3$ (the $\times$ key acts as $+$ and vice versa). Division and multiplication come first: $4\div12\times6=2$, so the result is $2+2+3=7$.

**Answer: 7**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-07.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-07.body:
Use coordinates (east, north) with the start at $(0,0)$. After the first leg she is at $(2,0)$. The second leg, bearing $210^\circ$, adds $2(\sin210^\circ,\cos210^\circ)=(-1,-\sqrt3)$, so she ends at $(1,-\sqrt3)$. Note the distance from the start is $\sqrt{1+3}=2$ km: the path is two sides of an equilateral triangle (the bearings differ by $120^\circ$, so the angle between the legs is $60^\circ$). To return she walks along $(-1,\sqrt3)$, which points $30^\circ$ west of north, i.e. bearing $360^\circ-30^\circ=330^\circ$.

**Answer: 330 degrees**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-08.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-08.body:
Let the flower bed have side $s$. The bed plus path form a square of side $s+2$, so the path has area $(s+2)^2-s^2=4s+4=72$, giving $s=17$. The flower bed has area $17^2=289$ m$^2$.

**Answer: 289 m$^2$**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-09.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-09.body:
Multiples of 4 are multiples of 2, so we remove multiples of 2 or 3. Multiples of 2: 50; of 3: 33; of 6 (both): 16. Removed: $50+33-16=67$. Remaining: $100-67=33$.

**Answer: 33**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-11.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-11.body:
After $n$ days the bank holds $1+2+4+\cdots+2^{n-1}=2^n-1$ pence. We need more than 500p: $2^9-1=511>500$ but $2^8-1=255<500$. So it is the 9th day: 26 May $+8$ days $=3$ June (26 May is day 1, 31 May is day 6, 3 June is day 9).

**Answer: 3 June**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-12.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-12.body:
$14\to7\to32\to16\to8\to4\to2\to1\to2\to1\ldots$ The different integers are $14,7,32,16,8,4,2,1$. The four smallest are $1,2,4,7$ with sum $14$.

**Answer: 14**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-13.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-13.body:
Gymnastics: $9+3=12$; athletics: $12+3=15$. Pupils watching at least one: $28-9=19$. Those watching both: $15+12-19=8$. Only gymnastics: $12-8=4$.

**Answer: 4**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-14.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-14.body:
Let the numbers be $a\le b\le c\le d$. Median 2 means $b+c=4$, so $(b,c)=(1,3)$ or $(2,2)$. Range 3 means $d=a+3$. If $(b,c)=(1,3)$ then $a=1$, $d=4$: set $1,1,3,4$ with mean $\frac94$. If $(2,2)$ then $a=1$ or $2$: sets $1,2,2,4$ (mean $\frac94$) and $2,2,2,5$ (mean $\frac{11}4$). The different values of $m$ are $\frac94$ and $\frac{11}4$, with sum $5$.

**Answer: 5**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-15.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-15.body:
Let the race be $d$ metres. Rear wheel turns: $\frac{d}{1.2}$; front: $\frac d{1.8}$. $\frac d{1.2}-\frac d{1.8}=150$, i.e. $d\left(\frac56-\frac59\right)=\frac{5d}{18}=150$, so $d=540$.

Check: $540/1.2=450$ turns and $540/1.8=300$ turns.

**Answer: 540 m**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-16.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-16.body:
She paid $8\times£5=£40$ (24 books in 8 groups of 3). The full price is $24\times1.99=£47.76$. The difference is $£7.76$.

**Answer: £7.76**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-17.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-17.body:
In order: $0,1,2,7$. The median is $\frac{1+2}2=1.5$ and the range is $7$. Product $=10.5$.

**Answer: 10.5**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-18.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-18.body:
The year (2017) has 365 days, i.e. $365\times24=8760$ hours. He is not standing for $5\%$ of this: $0.05\times8760=438$ hours.

**Answer: 438 hours**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-19.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-19.body:
Harry takes $\frac{21}{14}=1.5$ h $=90$ min; Martha takes $\frac{21}{12}=1.75$ h $=105$ min. Harry waits $105-90=15$ minutes.

**Answer: 15 minutes**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-20.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-20.body:
The riders are represented by $360-315=45^\circ$, which is $\frac18$ of the circle. $\frac18\times504=63$.

**Answer: 63**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-21.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-21.body:
The centre of the square is the midpoint of the diagonal $AC$: $(20,20)$. Reflecting in the $x$-axis changes the sign of the $y$-coordinate: $(20,-20)$.

**Answer: $(20,-20)$**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-22.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-22.body:
Old volume $=5\times6\times2=60$ cm$^3$. New volume $=1.8\times60=108$ cm$^3$.

**Answer: 108 cm$^3$**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-24.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-24.body:
The bearings differ by $120^\circ$, so the angle between the two legs of 35 m is $60^\circ$. An isosceles triangle with apex $60^\circ$ is equilateral, so $x=35$. With coordinates (east, north): leg 1 $=35(\sin260^\circ,\cos260^\circ)\approx(-34.5,-6.1)$ and leg 2 $=35(\sin140^\circ,\cos140^\circ)\approx(22.5,-26.8)$, so he is at about $(-12.0,-32.9)$. The way back is the vector $(12.0,32.9)$, which has bearing $\tan^{-1}(12.0/32.9)=20^\circ$, so $y=20$. (Geometrically: the directions of the legs are $260^\circ$ and $140^\circ$ and the third side of the equilateral triangle points at $20^\circ$, i.e. $140^\circ-120^\circ$.) Therefore $x+y=35+20=55$.

**Answer: 55**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-26.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-26.body:
The factors of 26 are $1,2,13,26$. Product $=1\times2\times13\times26=676$; sum $=42$. Difference $=634$.

**Answer: 634**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-27.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-27.body:
The sequence has $1+2+\cdots+8=36$ terms, so the median is the mean of the 18th and 19th terms. In increasing order the terms are: eight $-8$s (positions 1-8), six $-6$s (9-14), four $-4$s (15-18), two $-2$s (19-20), then the positive terms. The 18th term is $-4$ and the 19th is $-2$, so the median is $\frac{-4+(-2)}{2}=-3$.

**Answer: -3**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-28.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-28.body:
The total time is 6 hours, so the total distance is $2\times6=12$ miles. The distances are $1+4+3x$, so $5+3x=12$ and $x=\frac73$.

**Answer: $2\frac13$ mph**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-29.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-29.body:
$14\to7\to22\to11\to34\to17\to52\to26\to13\to40\to20\to10\to5\to16\to8\to4\to2\to1\to4\ldots$ The four smallest different numbers are $1,2,4,5$ with sum $12$.

**Answer: 12**

ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-30.title: Solution
ukmt-tmc-2017-regional-relay-30.body:
The triangle has a vertical leg of 3 cm and a horizontal leg of 12 cm along $AB$, so its height at distance $u$ from the vertical leg is $3-\frac u4$. The square is 8 cm wide (and taller than the triangle), so the overlap is the part of the triangle within a strip of width 8 cm. This is biggest when the strip covers the tallest part of the triangle, $0\le u\le8$: it is a trapezium with parallel sides $3$ and $1$ and width $8$, area $\frac{3+1}{2}\times8=16$ cm$^2$. (Any other position of the strip covers a thinner part.)

**Answer: 16 cm$^2$**
